title: SwiftVI: Faster Value Iteration via Heap-Based Action Elimination
problem: Standard value iteration (VI) for large Markov Decision Processes is computationally expensive because it updates all state-action pairs every iteration, even when most actions can be provably pruned.
motivation: Algorithms like BAO and AncVI reduce work but require full precomputation or have limited applicability; a heap-based approach exploiting monotone upper bounds on action values can prune actions without full precomputation and generalize across MDP structures.
method: For each state, it maintains a sorted ranking (max-heap) of upper-bound reward estimates for each possible action, and discards actions whose upper bounds fall below the current best lower bound after each update. It provides four variants combining different optimizations: VIH (heap only), VIAE (updating states one at a time rather than all together), VIAEH (combining both approaches), and VIAEHL (with a look-ahead step). All exploit the monotone nature of value estimates—they improve or stay constant across iterations—which ensures the action pruning is always correct.
key_novelty: It eliminates dominated actions using a sorted list of upper bounds during value iteration, relying on value estimates that only improve (never decrease) over iterations to avoid pre-analyzing the action space.
contributions: VIH algorithm: value iteration with per-state max-heap for action upper bound tracking
VIAE: asynchronous value iteration with incremental action elimination
VIAEH and VIAEHL: hybrid variants with lookahead for further pruning
Empirical validation showing consistent speedups over VI, IVI, BAO, AncVI on both random and real-world MDPs

metrics.speedup: VIH consistently best on random and real-world MDPs vs VI/IVI/BAO/AncVI; exact ratios depend on MDP structure

limitations: Speedup depends heavily on MDP structure (action space size, transition sparsity); heap overhead may dominate on small MDPs; not GPU-accelerated.
